name: THC Worked Example Visual Production Queue
purpose: Asset-level production tracking for worked-example visuals. Artwork status is independent from worked-example scientific approval and cannot authorize learner-facing publication.
approvalRule: A visual may be marked approved only after scientific, visual, label/spelling, accessibility, mobile, and placement QA all pass. Visual approval does not set learnerFacingApproved on the worked example.

items.title: Root decline after repeated wet irrigation
items.altText: Diagnostic decision diagram showing brown-root decline, root-zone measurements, pathogen evidence, competing abiotic causes, and a verification loop.
items.caption: Root decline is interpreted from plant pattern, root-zone conditions, organism evidence, and follow-up—not from root color alone.

items.title: VPD reading looks acceptable, leaves still show excessive demand
items.altText: Environmental measurement diagram comparing controller VPD with canopy and leaf conditions, including sensor placement, leaf temperature, light, airflow, and root-zone context.
items.caption: VPD is a derived metric whose interpretation depends on where and how temperature and humidity are measured and on actual leaf conditions.

items.title: A dryback percentage is copied from another facility
items.altText: Dryback measurement workflow showing different measurement bases, a post-irrigation reference, time-series change, sensor position, root-zone EC, and plant response.
items.caption: Dryback is a defined change over time, not a universal percentage that transfers unchanged between substrates, sensors, containers, and crops.

items.title: High center PPFD, weak edge growth
items.altText: Top-down PPFD grid showing center hotspots, edge low-light zones, fixture geometry, raw readings, and before-after mapping.
items.caption: Spatial light mapping shows whether averages hide crop-relevant hotspots or low-light zones.

items.title: Yellowing appears after a bloom-booster increase
items.altText: Differential-diagnosis board connecting yellowing symptoms with root condition, pH, EC, irrigation, recent nutrient changes, competing explanations, and verification.
items.caption: Deficiency-like symptoms require root-zone and management evidence before a nutrient correction is justified.

items.title: Clone matches genotype but performs differently
items.altText: Clone lineage diagram showing shared inherited genotype alongside differences in root quality, health, propagation history, environment, and phenotype.
items.caption: Clonal propagation preserves inherited genotype but not identical physiological state, health, or performance across conditions.

items.title: One photo is labeled a nutrient deficiency
items.altText: Plant diagnostic workflow moving from a leaf observation to whole-crop pattern, root-zone and environmental evidence, ranked hypotheses, and controlled verification.
items.caption: A strong plant diagnosis explains the crop pattern, survives competing explanations, and is verified after a bounded correction.

items.title: Dense flower rot is assumed to be Botrytis
items.altText: Disease differential diagram showing flower-rot symptoms, pathogen signs, canopy microclimate, diagnostic sampling, and confidence-based identification.
items.caption: Botrytis diagnosis is strongest when signs, disease pattern, environment, and diagnostic evidence agree.

items.title: Recurring pest problem despite calendar sprays
items.altText: Integrated pest management loop linking prevention, scouting, identification, decision thresholds, interventions, compatibility, and repeated verification.
items.caption: IPM is a recurring evidence-and-prevention system, not a calendar spray schedule.

items.title: Drying room setpoint is stable but batches dry unevenly
items.altText: Drying-room map showing rack positions, airflow paths, load density, spatial measurements, and different drying curves across zones.
items.caption: Drying uniformity must be checked across the actual load because room averages can hide position effects.

items.title: Small F2 population misses a rare trait combination
items.altText: F2 breeding diagram linking segregation and recombination with population size, recovery probability, observed classes, and model assumptions.
items.caption: Population size determines how well an F2 can sample rare favorable combinations under the stated genetic model.

items.title: One phenotype wins in one room
items.altText: Breeding trial comparison showing a confounded single-room result versus replicated blocked or randomized testing with checks and environmental retesting.
items.caption: Replication and environmental control help separate genetic signal from room and position effects.

items.title: New meter shows more decimal places
items.altText: Measurement-quality diagram comparing display resolution, reference accuracy, repeatability, bias, uncertainty, and supported reported digits.
items.caption: Extra decimal places describe resolution, not whether the measurement is accurate or fit for the decision.

items.title: One sensor is used to represent an entire room
items.altText: Sampling-plan diagram comparing one central sensor with a representative spatial grid and time-based measurements across room gradients.
items.caption: A sampling plan should represent the population and decision, not just produce many readings from one location.

items.title: Testing two irrigation strategies without pseudoreplication
items.altText: Experimental-design diagram contrasting a two-room pseudoreplicated comparison with independent treatment units, subsamples, randomization, and blocking.
items.caption: Replication is determined by independent treatment assignment, not by the number of measurements taken inside one treatment unit.

items.title: Higher light is correlated with higher yield
items.altText: Causal-reasoning diagram showing a light-yield correlation, alternative explanations, potential confounders, and stronger controlled designs.
items.caption: Correlation is useful evidence, but causal claims require designs that address timing and credible alternative explanations.
